note: Suites we run that EvalScope also implements. EvalScope names ModelScope mirrors as its dataset ids, but its adapters read the ORIGINAL Hugging Face column names, so a mirror is a straight copy and we can point each benchmark at our own pinned snapshot instead. That is what makes this a cross-check rather than a second measurement: both harnesses read byte-identical data at the same commit, so any disagreement is scoring, not data. We do not pull from ModelScope.

suites.note: EvalScope's dataset id is TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro already; same repo, same pin as ours.
Same repo and pin as ours. EvalScope grades HLE with a judge and we grade string-match-then-judge, so compare the delta and never the absolute.
EvalScope names AI-ModelScope/gpqa_diamond but its adapter reads 'Question', 'Correct Answer' and 'Incorrect Answer 1..3', which are Idavidrein's own column names. Pointed at our pin instead.
EvalScope evaluates the validation split; our suite scores 200 items of it.

Adapter reads id/question/options/answer/subject/topic_difficulty/image, which is MMMU_Pro's own schema. Its 'image' is the vision subset's single image where our adapter reads image_1..7 of the standard subset, so confirm which subset is loaded before trusting a comparison.

Schema matches (question_content, contest_date, evaluation_sample, format_prompt), so the data side is ready. Held back because scoring executes model-written code and EvalScope runs review inline on the generating machine; needs the sandbox engine settled first.

The only one needing real work. EvalScope's adapter reads a merged {question, ground_truth} record, while upstream ships prompts and possible_answer as separate files, so its mirror pre-merges them. Needs a custom dataset built from our pin. Its 17 subsets include every live_* category and multi_turn_*, which is more than we can score today.
